solver.kind: blind AI solver (separate agent, answer-free packet, rubric v2)

flags: minor: the colon clause (lacked skull and most of tail) almost defines 'fragmentary'; C and D are throwaway distractors, so only B is a real competitor and the context rules it out
S032-01.notes: Missing skull and tail means the specimen is incomplete, so 'fragmentary'. 'Intact' contradicts this; 'duplicate' and 'living' make no sense.

S032-02.notes: Waverers announced support and the bill passed, so the speech roused and unified them: galvanized. Alienated and bewildered are the opposite; outnumbered doesn't fit.

flags: minor: the 'Although the wall is extremely long' wording maps directly onto C's 'despite its great length', which makes it a near-lookup
S032-03.notes: Sentence 3 explains the reason (narrow, low contrast) for the difficulty reported in sentence 2. Fact check OK: the wall is not visible to the naked eye from the Moon, and it is very hard to see from low Earth orbit.

flags: minor: 'a form of nitrogen that is common in the ocean but rare on land' oversimplifies the science. The marker is nitrogen-15, a heavy isotope that is enriched in marine-derived nitrogen but still a minor isotope everywhere. 'Relatively more abundant in the ocean' would be more accurate.
S032-04.notes: Bears carry carcasses inland, and trees carry a marine nitrogen signature and grow faster, so salmon bring ocean nutrients. A ignores the bears (trees are not in ocean water); C is about bear growth, which isn't measured; D reverses the causation.

flags: minor: A is a strong trap because the virtual-tour drop alone looks supportive, but a claim about a gap needs both values for both groups
S032-05.notes: Gap for 18-29 is 45-38 = 7 points; for 65+ it is 55-14 = 41 points. Only D gives both values for both groups. A and B each give one column only; C covers the wrong group.

flags: minor: A closely paraphrases Text 2's last sentence ('inviting the listener'), which makes it near-lookup
S032-06.notes: The linguists find the rise on statements speakers are sure of, working as a comprehension check, so they would counter the 'uncertainty' view. B contradicts Text 2; C and D are unsupported.

S032-07.notes: The goal is to stress the length of the delay, and C gives the maximum (up to 17 hours). A stresses the short delay; B and D are off-goal. Fact check OK: Kabadayi & Osvath, Science 2017, ravens with 15-minute and 17-hour delays.

S032-08.notes: The text moves from 'no tailpipe emissions' to 'not emission-free over full life', a concession or contrast, so 'Even so'. Therefore, Likewise and In other words all misstate the relationship.

S032-09.notes: The introductory participial phrase 'Excavated...' must modify the body. Only B places the body as subject and gives a grammatical 'was so well preserved that'. A, C and D leave the modifier dangling or break the structure (A: 'peat cutters ... so well preserved'). Fact check OK: Tollund Man was found by peat cutters near Silkeborg in 1950, and they initially suspected a recent murder.

S032-10.notes: Two independent clauses are joined with 'however', so the correct form is 'May; however,'. A is a comma splice (a common trap); B has no punctuation before however; C is missing the comma after however.
